pulls.title: Use banker's rounding for money (ACC-7)
pulls.author: fede
pulls.body:
Closes #20.

Finance's ledger rounds half to even (accounting policy ACC-7). We round halves up, so about 3% of invoices miss reconciliation by a cent. `roundMoney` now sends exact ties to the even cent (0.125 -> 0.12, 0.875 -> 0.88), for every amount we round: charges, invoices, and refunds alike. Also adds `invoiceTotal` and exports it.

comments.author: dana
comments.body: Confirming for finance: ACC-7 applies to every amount we book, refunds included. The ledger is the source of truth.

pulls.title: Round negative amounts away from zero
pulls.author: bruno
pulls.body:
Fixes #18.

`Math.round` rounds halves towards +infinity, so -0.375 became -0.37 while 0.375 became 0.38. `roundMoney` now rounds the magnitude and puts the sign back, so a refund always mirrors its charge. Adds `refundTotal`.

issues.title: Refund rounds differently from the charge
issues.author: carla
issues.body: Charged $0.375 -> customer pays $0.38. Refund the same line -> refund receipt says -$0.37. Customers see a 1 cent mismatch. A refund must round to the same magnitude as its charge.

issues.title: Invoices fail ledger reconciliation by 1 cent
issues.author: dana
issues.body: The ledger follows ACC-7: amounts are rounded half to even (banker's rounding). We round half up, so ~3% of invoices are off by a cent and need manual fixes each month. Please round every booked amount the ACC-7 way.
